description: Migrate SIP trunking from the current carrier (Carrier A) to a new carrier (Carrier B) for an enterprise VoIP system handling 5000 concurrent calls. The migration must follow: number porting (submit porting request to Carrier B — this is an external, irreversible provisioning step handled by the carrier and cannot be rolled back once the port completes), configure the new SIP trunk on Carrier B, run dual-trunk period (both trunks active, inbound calls route to both, outbound via Carrier B), execute cutover (inbound routing switches to Carrier B only, decommission Carrier A trunk), verify (call completion rate, audio quality, DTMF, fax/POS modem compatibility), and release the old carrier. A rollback plan must exist for the cutover step (re-route inbound to Carrier A) but NOT for number porting (once ported, the numbers belong to Carrier B — this is the irreversible external step). Risk factors: number porting is irreversible and carrier-controlled (outside the private environment), porting can fail mid-way leaving numbers in limbo, and SIP codec/DTMF differences between carriers. Tools available: SIP PBX (Asterisk/FreeSWITCH), carrier portal, SBC (Session Border Controller), Wireshark (SIP tracing), monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana).
